# Architecture

Crossfoot is one Python package with a command-line entry point, files on disk, and a static results page. No
server, no database server, no queue. Each part below names the requirement in `.prod-build/contract.md` that forces it.

## The idea in one paragraph

A scanned table prints its own totals. If every cell is read into a ledger, each value can be tested twice: its
row has to add up to the total printed at the end of the row, and its column has to add up to the total printed
under the column. One wrong cell fails both sums, and the two failing sums cross at it. Crossfoot reads the scan
with a vision model, accepts a value only when both sums hold, re-reads the cells where they do not, and then uses
the closed ledger to audit a published file that was copied from the same scan.

## Layout of the repository

```
crossfoot/
  cli.py        command-line entry point (argparse): audit, read, verify-known, budget, site
  sources.py    the eight benchmark counties: scan URL, published-file URL, cache under data/ (M1, M4)
  render.py     pdftoppm wrapper: page -> PNG at a dpi; crops with Pillow (M1, M3)
  segment.py    finds blocks and column lines on a ruled page from the image itself (M1)
  model.py      gateway client, JSON parsing with one repair attempt, cost meter, budget guard, rate limit (M7)
  tracing.py    neatlogs setup and span helpers; a no-op when the key is absent (M7)
  layouts/
    matrix.py   precincts as columns, three rows per candidate, totals both ways (Panola)
    report.py   one precinct per page, one row per candidate with its own total (San Saba, Cottle and others)
    profile.py  decides which layout a county uses and tests the decision on the first pages (M1)
  ledger.py     SQLite ledger: cells, printed totals, checks, events; resume (M2, M6)
  checks.py     row sums, column sums, grand totals, grid completeness; pure functions (M2)
  agent.py      the investigation loop: a model chooses the next action for each open item; code enforces the rules (M3)
  audit.py      compares the closed ledger with the published file; classifies and settles disagreements (M4)
  outputs.py    county.json, findings.json, corrected CSV, report.md, the site's data bundle (M5, M8)
  policy.py     the one stored answer and its default (S1)
tests/          unit tests for checks, ledger, audit, budget, resume, agent rules; no network
site/           the static results page (plain HTML, CSS and JS; no build step) (M8)
runs/           one folder per run; small results are committed, caches are not
data/           downloaded scans and files; never committed
```

## Inputs

Eight Texas counties from the OpenElections project's 2024 general election benchmark. All eight scans are
image-only PDFs (no text layer): Cottle 12 pages, Foard 16, Jones 20, Limestone 42, Lynn 37, Panola 6, San Saba 21,
Scurry 38.

- Scan: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-sources-tx/master/2024/general/2024%20<County>%20County%2C%20TX%20precinct-level%20results.pdf`
- Published file: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-data-tx/master/2024/counties/20241105__tx__general__<county>__precinct.csv`
  with columns `county, precinct, office, district, party, candidate, votes, absentee, early_voting, election_day`.

## Two layouts

**Matrix (Panola).** A landscape canvass sheet. The header row lists the precincts as columns and ends in a TOTAL
column. Each candidate is a block: a label at the left, three ruled rows (EARLY, ABSENTEE, PRECINCT), a row of
small printed totals under the columns, and a grand total under the TOTAL column. In the published file EARLY is
`early_voting`, ABSENTEE is `absentee`, PRECINCT is `election_day`, and the small total is `votes`.
Checks per block: for each precinct, early + absentee + precinct = the small total; for each row, the precinct cells
add to the row's TOTAL; the small totals add to the grand total.

**Report (San Saba, Cottle and others).** One precinct per page or section. Each candidate is a row with four
numbers: TOTAL, Absentee, Early Voting, Election Day. Checks per row: total = absentee + early + election day.
Where the page prints a total for the contest, the candidates' totals have to add to it.

`layouts/profile.py` asks the model which layout the first page shows and what the column order is, then reads the
first page under that layout and runs the checks. A profile under which more than a third of the sums fail is
rejected; the other layout is tried; if neither holds the county is reported as "layout not supported" and left alone.

## Reading

1. `render.py` renders a page at 200 dpi.
2. Matrix: `segment.py` finds the blocks as bands of ink separated by blank bands, and the column lines inside a
   block as columns of dark pixels that run the height of the ruled rows. Report: the page is read whole.
3. Matrix: each block is cut into column groups no wider than 1,500 px at 300 dpi, one model call per group; report:
   one page per call. The answer is strict JSON, validated (right number of columns, integers only), with one repair
   request. Every value comes back with the block, row kind and column it belongs to.
4. Which model reads a county is decided by measurement, not fixed. A sample of the first page is read with
   `claude-haiku`; if more than a tenth of the sample's row sums fail, the county is read with `claude-sonnet-4.6`.
   Measured on Panola on 11 October 2026, same code and crops: `claude-haiku` left 85 of 943 printed sums failing
   (44 after a 20-minute re-read loop with 565 more calls); `claude-sonnet-4.6` left 6 of 942.
5. The values go into the ledger as `first_read`, with the page and the pixel box of each value where it is known.

## The ledger (`ledger.py`, SQLite, one file per run)

- `cells(county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, first_read, status, tries, model, x0, y0, x1, y1)`
  with status in `first_read | accepted | failed | cannot_verify`.
- `totals(county, page, block_id, direction, key, value)` for printed row totals, column totals and grand totals.
- `events(ts, county, kind, payload_json)` for everything the agent did, in order. The results page replays these.
- A county is `closed` when every sum holds and the grid has no gap, or every open cell is `cannot_verify`.
- Resume: on start, accepted cells are kept and only open ones are worked on.

## Checks (`checks.py`, no model, no I/O)

Pure functions over the ledger's rows. They return, for each sum, its terms, the printed total, the computed total
and pass or fail, and for each failing cell the sums that cross at it. `locate()` returns the cells that sit on a
failing row sum and a failing column sum at once. Grid completeness lists every precinct, contest and candidate that
is present in one place and absent in another.

## The investigation loop (`agent.py`)

Every value on a matrix sheet sits on two printed sums. A cell sits on its row and its column. The small total under
a column sits on that column and on the grand total (the small totals add to it). A row's printed total sits on its
row and on the grand total (the three row totals add to it). So one wrong value makes exactly two sums fail, and they
cross at it. `checks.suspects()` pairs failing sums that share one value and whose differences agree: that value is
the suspect, and the difference says what it would have to be. (The grand total is checked two ways, kinds `grand_col`
and `grand_row`. The registered-voters row of Panola sits on one sum only and cannot be located this way.)

The loop works the sums that still fail after the first read, and later every disagreement with the published file.
For a located suspect it looks at the scan again: a re-read of that one value, cut at 400 dpi or more and enlarged.
A value changes only because a re-read of the scan gave the new value; arithmetic says where to look, never what to
write. What pairing cannot locate goes to the model, which is shown the failing sums and what has been tried and
returns one action as JSON:

- `reread {target, dpi, model}`: a single value, a column slice or a row strip
- `conclude {item, verdict, reason}`: `document_inconsistent` or `cannot_verify`
- `ask_policy {question_id}`: use the stored answer, or the default marked as unconfirmed
- `done {item}`

Rules that code enforces whatever the model says: at most six actions per item; re-reads climb one step at a time
(the county's reader, then `claude-sonnet-4.6`, then `claude-opus-4.6`), a step only after the one below has failed
to settle the value; the same target is never re-read twice with the same model and dpi; no value is accepted unless
both of its sums hold; a value the scan shows the same way twice while its two sums still fail is
`document_inconsistent` (the document disagrees with itself there) and the stored policy answer applies; a correction
is written only when the printed totals agree with the new value and disagree with the old one.
Every action and its result is an event in the ledger and a span in neatlogs.

## The audit (`audit.py`)

1. Load the published file. Normalise labels (case, punctuation, party suffixes, running mates).
2. Map the scan's contests and candidates to the file's. Exact and normalised matches first; what is left goes to
   the model once per county as two lists, and code checks that the answer is one-to-one and that mapped pairs have
   close county totals.
3. Compare cell by cell. A disagreement is classified:
   `file_row_fails_own_total`, `wrong_number`, `wrong_column`, `wrong_precinct`, `missing_row`, `extra_row`.
4. Settle it. If the scan's value passes both of its sums and the file's value breaks a printed total, the status is
   `settled_against_file`. If no printed total can decide, `cannot_verify`. If the scan's own totals disagree with
   its cells, `document_inconsistent`, and the stored policy answer applies.
5. Keep the evidence: the crop of the block, the sums with their terms, the old and the new value.
   Every finding carries `confirmed_by_person: false` until a person changes it.

## Outputs (`outputs.py`)

`runs/<run_id>/run.json` (start, end, commit, model calls, tokens, cost, counties), and per county
`county.json` (cells, totals, checks, events), `findings.json`, `crops/*.png`, `corrected/<published file name>`,
`changes.diff` and `report.md`. `crossfoot site build --run <id>` copies what the results page needs into
`site/data/`: `index.json`, one JSON per county, the page images that carry findings (at most 1600 px wide) and the crops.

## Tracing and cost (`tracing.py`, `model.py`)

`neatlogs.init(api_key=..., workflow_name="crossfoot")`; the gateway client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap(OpenAI(...))`.
A county run is a `WORKFLOW` span, the loop is an `AGENT` span, each tool is a `TOOL` span
(`@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name=...)`), tagged with run, county, page, block and cell. `neatlogs.flush()` and
`neatlogs.shutdown()` run at exit. The cost meter adds up each response's token usage, and `crossfoot budget` reads
the gateway's own figure for the key (`GET <gateway root>/key/info`, where the root is `LITELLM_BASE_URL` without
`/v1`). The guard refuses a call that would pass the limit.

## The results page (`site/`)

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules, no framework and no build step, so it deploys as static files. It reads
`site/data/`. The scan is an image inside a container with CSS perspective; cells, sums and marks are DOM and SVG
elements placed in the image's own coordinates, so they tilt with it and stay real, selectable elements.
`UI-SPEC.md` is the specification.

## What can fail and what happens

| Dependency | Failure | What the program does |
|---|---|---|
| Model gateway | rate limit, timeout | waits and retries once, then marks the item cannot-verify |
| Model gateway | budget reached | stops before the call, writes what it has, exits with a clear message |
| Model answer | not valid JSON, wrong column count | one repair request, then the block is marked failed and goes to the loop |
| Scan or file | cannot be downloaded | that county stops with the URL; other counties continue |
| neatlogs | key missing or unreachable | the run continues untraced and says so on its first line |
| Position finding | no ruled lines | crops fall back to whole blocks and the page shows crops without cell marks |

## Decisions

- SQLite for the ledger, because a stopped run has to resume and the page replays events in order.
- A JSON action protocol for the loop instead of provider tool-calling, so it runs unchanged on any model the gateway serves.
- CSS 3D for the stage instead of WebGL: the sheet is the only object, text has to stay crisp and selectable, and
  the page has to work with the effect off.

140	        if not isinstance(d, dict) or not isinstance(d.get("rows"), dict):
141	            raise ValueError("answer must be an object with a 'rows' object")
142	        for r in rows + tuple(extra):
143	            if r not in d["rows"]:
144	                raise ValueError(f"row {r} is missing")
145	            _check_list(d["rows"][r].get("values"), n, f"{r} values")
146	            _int_or_none(d["rows"][r].get("total"), f"{r} total")
147	        _check_list(d.get("col_totals"), n, "col_totals")
148	        _int_or_none(d.get("grand"), "grand")
149	    return check

152	def header_validator(d):
153	    p = d.get("precincts")
154	    if not isinstance(p, list) or not p:
155	        raise ValueError("precincts must be a non-empty list")
156	    d["precincts"] = [str(x).strip() for x in p]
157	    if len(set(d["precincts"])) != len(d["precincts"]):
158	        raise ValueError("precinct labels must be distinct")
159	    n = len(p)
160	    _check_list(d.get("registered", {}).get("values"), n, "registered values")
161	    validator(n)(d)

164	def _edges(blocks, n):
165	    """Column edges for a page: from the first block with n+2 lines: the left edge of the row-label box, then the n+1
166	    precinct edges (the last is TOTAL's left edge). Returns those n+1 edges."""
167	    for b in blocks:
168	        if len(b.lines) == n + 2:
169	            return b.lines[1:n + 2]
170	    return None

173	def _box(edges, b, row_i, col_i):
174	    if edges is None:
175	        return (None,) * 4
176	    h = (b.rule_y1 - b.rule_y0) / len(ROWS)
177	    return (edges[col_i], round(b.rule_y0 + row_i * h), edges[col_i + 1], round(b.rule_y0 + (row_i + 1) * h))

180	def _store(led, county, page, bid, d, cols, contest, candidate, model, edges, b):
181	    """Write one block's answer: cells (null = blacked out, no cell) and printed totals. Returns cells stored."""
182	    stored = 0
183	    for ri, r in enumerate(ROWS):
184	        for ci, col in enumerate(cols):
185	            v = d["rows"][r]["values"][ci]
186	            if v is None:
187	                continue
188	            led.put_cell(county, page, bid, r, col, v, contest=contest, candidate=candidate, model=model,
189	                         box=_box(edges, b, ri, ci) if edges else (None,) * 4)
190	            stored += 1
191	        if d["rows"][r]["total"] is not None:
192	            led.put_total(county, page, bid, "row", r, d["rows"][r]["total"])
193	    for ci, col in enumerate(cols):
194	        if d["col_totals"][ci] is not None:
195	            led.put_total(county, page, bid, "col", col, d["col_totals"][ci])
196	    if d["grand"] is not None:
197	        led.put_total(county, page, bid, "grand", "", d["grand"])
198	    return stored

202	    n = 0
203	    for ci, col in enumerate(cols):
204	        led.put_cell(county, page, "reg", "REGISTERED", col, d["registered"]["values"][ci], contest="Registered voters",
205	                     model=model)

208	        led.put_total(county, page, "reg", "row", "REGISTERED", d["registered"]["total"])
209	    n += _store(led, county, page, "cast", d, cols, "Ballots cast", None, model, None, None)

213	def summarize(led, county):
214	    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
215	    rows, cols, grand = (checks.row_checks(cells, totals), checks.column_checks(cells, totals),
216	                         checks.grand_checks(totals))
217	    ok = lambda cs: sum(c.ok for c in cs)
218	    return {"cells_read": len(cells), "failed_cells": sum(c["status"] == "failed" for c in cells),
219	            "row_sums_pass": ok(rows), "row_sums_fail": len(rows) - ok(rows),
220	            "col_sums_pass": ok(cols), "col_sums_fail": len(cols) - ok(cols),
221	            "grand_sums_pass": ok(grand), "grand_sums_fail": len(grand) - ok(grand),
222	            "printed_totals": len(totals)}

225	def _read_block(gw, county, page, bid, b, edges, cols, png, crop_path, run_id, root, dpi):
226	    """One answer for the block: one call on the whole crop when the page gives no column edges, else one per group."""
227	    if edges is None:
228	        g = Group(0, len(cols), True, True, b.x1 - b.x0)
229	        return gw.ask_json(block_prompt(g, cols), crop_path, validate=validator(len(cols)))
230	    scale = READ_DPI / dpi
231	    hi = page_png(county, page, READ_DPI, root)
232	    groups = plan_groups(edges, b.x0, b.x1, scale=scale, max_w=MAX_WIDTH)
233	    answers = []
234	    for k, g in enumerate(groups):
235	        path = group_image(hi, b, edges, g, scale,
236	                           Path("runs") / run_id / "crops" / f"{bid}-g{k}.png" if run_id else Path(f"/tmp/{bid}-g{k}.png"))
237	        with Image.open(path) as im:
238	            w, h = im.size
239	        before = gw.cost
240	        with tracing.trace("read_group", kind="TOOL", run=run_id, county=county, page=page, block=bid, group=k,
241	                           col_first=g.c0, col_last=g.c1 - 1, crop_width=w, crop_height=h, dpi=READ_DPI) as sp:
242	            answers.append(gw.ask_json(block_prompt(g, cols[g.c0:g.c1]), path, validate=validator(g.c1 - g.c0)))
243	            sp.set_attribute("estimated_cost_usd", round(gw.cost - before, 5))
244	    return merge_groups(answers)

247	def _rows_in(led, county):
248	    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
249	    chs = checks.row_checks(cells, totals)
250	    return len(chs), sum(1 for c in chs if not c.ok)

253	def read_county(county, gw, led, *, run_id="", pages=None, dpi=200, log=print, data_root=None, model="auto") -> dict:
254	    """Read every page of a matrix-layout county block by block into the ledger. Returns the summary dict.
255	
256	    model="auto": a sample of page 1 is read with claude-haiku first and the reader is chosen by the share of its row
257	    sums that fail (layouts/profile.py); the sample always comes from page 1, whatever `pages` says. Any other name
258	    reads the county with that model and skips the sample."""
259	    from ..sources import DATA
260	    from . import profile
261	    root = data_root or DATA
262	    t0 = time.time()
263	    pages = list(pages or range(1, 7))
264	    st = {"cols": None, "contest": None, "failed": 0, "log": [], "done": set()}
265	    stopped, sample = None, None
266	    blocks_of: dict = {}
267	
268	    def blocks_for(page):
269	        if page not in blocks_of:
270	            blocks_of[page] = find_blocks(page_png(county, page, dpi, root))
271	        return blocks_of[page]
272	
273	    def read_blocks(page, stop_when=None):
274	        """Read the blocks of one page not read yet. Stops early when `stop_when()` is true after a block."""
275	        png = page_png(county, page, dpi, root)
276	        blocks = blocks_for(page)
277	        for i, b in enumerate(blocks):
278	            bid = f"p{page}-b{i}"
279	            is_header = page == 1 and i == 0
280	            if bid in st["done"] or (page not in pages and not is_header and not stop_when):
281	                continue
282	            crop_path = Path("runs") / run_id / "crops" / f"{bid}.png" if run_id else Path(f"/tmp/{bid}.png")
283	            crop(png, b.box, crop_path)
284	            st["done"].add(bid)
285	            try:
286	                with tracing.trace("read_block", kind="TOOL", run=run_id, county=county, page=page, block=bid):
287	                    if is_header:
288	                        d = gw.ask_json(HEADER_PROMPT, crop_path, validate=header_validator)
289	                        st["cols"] = d["precincts"]
290	                        n = _store_header(led, county, page, d, st["cols"], gw.model)
291	                        what = "header"
292	                    else:
293	                        edges = _edges(blocks, len(st["cols"]))
294	                        d = _read_block(gw, county, page, bid, b, edges, st["cols"], png, crop_path, run_id, root, dpi)
295	                        st["contest"] = d.get("contest") or st["contest"]
296	                        n = _store(led, county, page, bid, d, st["cols"], st["contest"], d.get("candidate"), gw.model,
297	                                   edges, b)
298	                        what = d.get("candidate")
299	                led.event(county, "block_read", {"page": page, "block": bid, "cells": n, "candidate": what,
300	                                                 "model": gw.model})
301	                st["log"].append({"block": bid, "page": page, "status": "read", "cells": n, "candidate": what,
302	                                  "box": list(b.box)})
303	            except BudgetExceeded:
304	                raise
305	            except Exception as e:  # bad JSON twice, wrong shape, or a model error: mark the block failed, go on
306	                st["failed"] += 1
307	                if st["cols"]:
308	                    for r in ROWS:
309	                        for col in st["cols"]:
310	                            led.put_cell(county, page, bid, r, col, None, model=gw.model)
311	                            led.set_status(county, page, bid, r, col, "failed")
312	                led.event(county, "block_failed", {"page": page, "block": bid, "error": str(e)[:300]})
313	                st["log"].append({"block": bid, "page": page, "status": "failed", "error": str(e)[:300]})
314	                log(f"  {bid}: failed ({str(e)[:100]})")
315	                if is_header:
316	                    raise RuntimeError("the page-1 header could not be read; later pages need its precinct order")
317	            if stop_when and stop_when():
318	                return
319	
320	    try:
321	        with tracing.trace("read_county", kind="WORKFLOW", run=run_id, county=county):
322	            # the header row is printed on page 1 only (checked by eye); later pages reuse its precinct order
323	            if model == "auto":
324	                gw.model = profile.SAMPLE_MODEL
325	                read_blocks(1, stop_when=lambda: _rows_in(led, county)[0] >= profile.SAMPLE_ROW_SUMS)
326	                with tracing.trace("choose_reader", kind="TOOL", run=run_id, county=county) as sp:
327	                    total, failing = _rows_in(led, county)
328	                    sample = profile.decide(failing, total)
329	                    sample["blocks"] = sorted(st["done"])
330	                    for k in ("row_sums", "failing", "rate", "reader", "kept_sample"):
331	                        sp.set_attribute(f"sample_{k}" if k != "reader" else "choice", sample[k])
332	                led.event(county, "choose_reader", sample)
333	                log(profile.sentence(sample))
334	                gw.model = sample["reader"]
335	                if not sample["kept_sample"]:
336	                    led.clear_values(county)
337	                    st.update(cols=None, contest=None, failed=0, log=[], done=set())
338	            else:
339	                gw.model = model
340	                sample = {"reader": model, "skipped": True, "kept_sample": False}
341	                led.event(county, "choose_reader", sample)
342	                log(f"reader: {model} (set with --model; no sample was read)")
343	            for page in sorted(set(pages) | {1}):
344	                read_blocks(page)
345	    except BudgetExceeded as e:
346	        stopped = str(e)
347	        log(f"stopped: {e}")
348	    s = summarize(led, county)
349	    found = sum(len(blocks_for(p)) for p in pages)
350	    s.update(county=county, run_id=run_id, blocks_found=found, blocks_failed=st["failed"], reader=gw.model,
351	             sample=sample, precincts=st["cols"], model_calls=gw.calls, prompt_tokens=gw.prompt_tokens,
352	             completion_tokens=gw.completion_tokens, metered_cost_estimate=round(gw.cost, 4),
353	             seconds=round(time.time() - t0, 1), stopped=stopped, blocks=st["log"])
354	    return s

357	# ---- where things are on the page (for re-reads and for the results page); boxes are in 200 dpi pixels ----
358	
359	HEADER_ROWS = ("REGISTERED",) + ROWS + ("SMALL",)   # page 1's first block: one more row, and its small
360	# totals sit inside the ruled box, as its last row
361	GEO_DPI = 200
362	PAD = 8             # pixels of page around a crop, at 200 dpi
363	SMALL_ROW = 30      # height of the row of small printed totals under the ruled rows, at 200 dpi
364	MIN_DIGIT_PX = 40   # a re-read crop is enlarged until its digits are at least this tall
365	# printed digit height at 200 dpi, measured by eye on the Panola scan: cells and large totals about 10 px, the small
366	# totals about 6 px
367	DIGIT_200 = {"cell": 10, "row_total": 10, "grand": 10, "col_total": 6, "column": 6}
368	
369	
370	def digit_px(dpi: int, kind: str) -> float:
371	    return DIGIT_200[kind] * dpi / GEO_DPI
372	
373	
374	def scale_for(dpi: int, kind: str) -> float:
375	    return max(1.0, round(MIN_DIGIT_PX / digit_px(dpi, kind) + 0.01, 2))
376	
377	
378	class GeometryError(Exception):
379	    pass
380	
381	
382	class Geometry:
383	    """Boxes of cells, printed totals and blocks of one matrix-layout county, and crops of them from the scan."""
384	
385	    def __init__(self, county, cols, root=None):
386	        from ..sources import DATA
387	        self.county, self.cols, self.root = county, list(cols), root or DATA
388	        self._pages: dict = {}
389	        self._rule_cache: dict = {}
390	        self._cur_page = None
391	
392	    def _page(self, page):
393	        if page not in self._pages:
394	            blocks = find_blocks(page_png(self.county, page, GEO_DPI, self.root))
395	            self._pages[page] = (blocks, _edges(blocks, len(self.cols)))
396	        return self._pages[page]
397	
398	    def _block(self, page, bid):
399	        blocks, edges = self._page(page)
400	        i = 0 if bid in ("reg", "cast") else int(bid.rsplit("-b", 1)[1])
401	        if i >= len(blocks) or edges is None:
402	            raise GeometryError(f"no column lines found for {bid} on page {page}")
403	        rows = HEADER_ROWS if bid in ("reg", "cast") else ROWS
404	        self._cur_page = page
405	        self._rules(blocks[i], edges)
406	        return blocks[i], edges, rows
407	
408	    def _rules(self, b, edges):
409	        """y of each horizontal rule across the precinct columns inside the block's ruled height, found in the image."""
410	        key = (b.y0, b.x0)
411	        if key not in self._rule_cache:
412	            import numpy as np
413	            png = page_png(self.county, self._cur_page, GEO_DPI, self.root)
414	            with Image.open(png) as im:
415	                g = np.asarray(im.convert("L"))[b.rule_y0 - 3:b.rule_y1 + 4, edges[0]:edges[-2]]
416	            cover = (g < 110).mean(axis=1) >= 0.6
417	            ys = []
418	            for s_, e_ in segment._runs(cover):
419	                ys.append(b.rule_y0 - 3 + (s_ + e_) // 2)
420	            self._rule_cache[key] = ys
421	        return self._rule_cache[key]
422	
423	    def _row(self, b, rows, kind):
424	        i = rows.index(kind)
425	        ys = self._rule_cache.get((b.y0, b.x0)) or []
426	        h = (b.rule_y1 - b.rule_y0) / len(rows)
427	
428	        def edge(j):    # an even split, moved onto a drawn rule when one lies within 5 px
429	            y = b.rule_y0 + j * h
430	            near = min(ys, key=lambda r: abs(r - y), default=None)
431	            return round(near if near is not None and abs(near - y) <= 5 else y)
432	        return edge(i), edge(i + 1)
433	
434	    def block_box(self, page, bid):
435	        try:
436	            return self._block(page, bid)[0].box
437	        except GeometryError:
438	            return None
439	
440	    def cell_box(self, page, bid, row, col):
441	        b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
442	        y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, row)
443	        ci = self.cols.index(col)
444	        return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], y1)
445	
446	    def total_box(self, page, bid, direction, key):
447	        try:
448	            b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
449	            n = len(self.cols)
450	            if direction == "row":
451	                y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, key)
452	                return (edges[n], y0, b.x1, y1)
453	            if bid == "reg":
454	                return None
455	            if direction == "col":
456	                ci = self.cols.index(key)
457	                if bid == "cast":
458	                    y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, "SMALL")
459	                    return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], y1)
460	                return (edges[ci], b.rule_y1, edges[ci + 1], min(b.y1, b.rule_y1 + SMALL_ROW))
461	            if bid == "cast":
462	                y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, "SMALL")
463	                return (edges[n], y0, b.x1, b.y1)
464	            return (edges[n], b.rule_y1, b.x1, b.y1)
465	        except (GeometryError, ValueError):
466	            return None
467	
468	    def target_box(self, page, bid, t):
469	        """The box of a re-read target, without padding."""
470	        b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
471	        kind = t["kind"]
472	        if kind == "cell":
473	            return self.cell_box(page, bid, t["row"], t["column"])
474	        if kind == "column":
475	            ci = self.cols.index(t["column"])
476	            y0 = self._row(b, rows, "EARLY")[0]
477	            if bid == "cast":
478	                return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], self._row(b, rows, "SMALL")[1])
479	            return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], min(b.y1, b.rule_y1 + SMALL_ROW))
480	        if kind == "row_total":
481	            return self.total_box(page, bid, "row", t["row"])
482	        if kind == "col_total":
483	            return self.total_box(page, bid, "col", t["column"])
484	        if kind == "grand":
485	            return self.total_box(page, bid, "grand", "")
486	        raise GeometryError(f"unknown target kind {kind!r}")
487	
488	    def crop(self, page, bid, t, dpi, dest: Path):
489	        """Cut the target out of the page at `dpi`, with padding, enlarged so its digits are at least 40 px tall.
490	        Returns (path, box at 200 dpi)."""
491	        try:
492	            box = self.target_box(page, bid, t)
493	        except ValueError:
494	            box = None
495	        if box is None:
496	            raise GeometryError(f"cannot place {t} in {bid} on page {page}")
497	        return self._cut(page, box, t["kind"], dpi, dest), box
498	
499	    def _cut(self, page, box, kind, dpi, dest: Path) -> Path:
500	        k = dpi / GEO_DPI
501	        x0, y0, x1, y1 = box
502	        with Image.open(page_png(self.county, page, dpi, self.root)) as im:
503	            win = (max(0, round((x0 - PAD) * k)), max(0, round((y0 - PAD) * k)),
504	                   min(im.width, round((x1 + PAD) * k)), min(im.height, round((y1 + PAD) * k)))
505	            c = im.crop(win)
506	        s = scale_for(dpi, kind)
507	        if s > 1:
508	            c = c.resize((round(c.width * s), round(c.height * s)), Image.LANCZOS)
509	        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
510	        c.save(dest)
511	        return dest
512	
513	    def strip_crops(self, page, bid, row, dpi, dest: Path, per: int = 7):
514	        """One row of one block cut into pieces of at most `per` cells. Returns [(path, [precincts], box at 200 dpi)]."""
515	        try:
516	            b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
517	            if row not in rows:
518	                raise GeometryError(f"no row {row} in {bid}")
519	            y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, row)
520	            out = []
521	            for i in range(0, len(self.cols), per):
522	                cols = self.cols[i:i + per]
523	                box = (edges[i], y0, edges[i + len(cols)], y1)
524	                out.append((self._cut(page, box, "cell", dpi, dest.with_name(f"{dest.stem}-s{i // per}{dest.suffix}")),
525	                            cols, box))
526	            return out
527	        except (ValueError, IndexError):
528	            raise GeometryError(f"cannot place row {row} in {bid} on page {page}") from None
529	
530	
531	def precinct_order(led, county) -> list[str]:
532	    """The precinct columns left to right, as the header block's registered-voters row was read."""
533	    seen = []
534	    for c in led.cells(county):
535	        if c["block_id"] == "reg" and c["column"] not in seen:
536	            seen.append(c["column"])
537	    return seen

"""Matrix layout (Panola): precincts as columns, three ruled rows per candidate, totals both ways.

First read only: one crop per block goes to the model, the answer goes into the ledger as `first_read`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image

from .. import checks, tracing
from ..model import BudgetExceeded
from ..render import crop, page_png
from .. import segment
from ..segment import find_blocks

ROWS = ("EARLY", "ABSENTEE", "PRECINCT")
TOTAL = "TOTAL"

HEADER_PROMPT = """This image is the top of a landscape election canvass sheet. It has a header row of precinct
numbers ending in TOTAL, then a registered-voters row, then a ballots-cast block with rows EARLY, ABSENTEE and
PRECINCT, then a row of small totals under the columns and a grand total under TOTAL.
Answer with strict JSON only, no prose:
{"precincts": [precinct labels left to right, as printed, excluding TOTAL],
 "registered": {"values": [one integer per precinct], "total": integer},
 "rows": {"EARLY": {"values": [...], "total": integer}, "ABSENTEE": {...}, "PRECINCT": {...}},
 "col_totals": [the small printed total under each precinct, integers],
 "grand": the grand total under the TOTAL column}
Read digits exactly as printed. Every list has one entry per precinct, in order."""

BLOCK_PROMPT = """This image is {part} of one block of a landscape election canvass sheet. {labels}Its rows, top to
bottom, are EARLY, ABSENTEE and PRECINCT, with one cell per precinct, then under them a row of small printed totals
for each column. {total}There are {n} precinct columns in this image, in this order: {precincts}. A solid black cell
means the candidate is not in that precinct: use null for it, not 0.
Answer with strict JSON only, no prose:
{{"contest": {contest},
 "candidate": {candidate},
 "rows": {{"EARLY": {{"values": [{n} integers or null], "total": {tot}}},
          "ABSENTEE": {{"values": [{n} integers or null], "total": {tot}}},
          "PRECINCT": {{"values": [{n} integers or null], "total": {tot}}}}},
 "col_totals": [{n} integers or null: the small printed total under each column],
 "grand": {grand}}}
Read digits exactly as printed; do not correct or add anything up. Keep every value in the column it is printed in."""

READ_DPI = 300      # a printed digit is about 16 px tall here, against about 10 px at 200 dpi
MAX_WIDTH = 1500    # widest image sent to the model, in pixels at READ_DPI; wider ones are shrunk by the provider


def block_prompt(g, precincts):
    return BLOCK_PROMPT.format(
        n=len(precincts), precincts=", ".join(precincts),
        part="the whole" if g.labels and g.total else "a column group",
        labels=("The candidate's name is at the left (a contest title may appear above or beside it). "
                if g.labels else "The candidate's name is not in this image. "),
        total=("The last printed number at the end of each row is that row's TOTAL, and a grand total is printed "
               "under the TOTAL column at the far right. " if g.total else
               "The row TOTAL column is not in this image. "),
        contest='"the contest title if one is printed in this image, else null"' if g.labels else "null",
        candidate='"the candidate\'s name as printed, with party in brackets if shown"' if g.labels else "null",
        tot="integer" if g.total else "null", grand="the grand total under the TOTAL column" if g.total else "null")


@dataclass
class Group:
    c0: int
    c1: int          # columns c0..c1-1
    labels: bool     # includes the row-label strip at the left
    total: bool      # includes the TOTAL strip at the right
    width: float     # pixels at the read dpi


def plan_groups(edges, label_x0, total_x1, *, scale, max_w) -> list[Group]:
    """Cut the columns (n+1 edges) into runs whose image, with labels in the first and TOTAL in the last, fits max_w."""
    n = len(edges) - 1
    label_w = (edges[0] - label_x0) * scale
    total_w = (total_x1 - edges[n]) * scale
    out, c = [], 0
    while c < n:
        first = c == 0
        w = label_w if first else 0.0
        c1 = c
        while c1 < n:
            nw = w + (edges[c1 + 1] - edges[c1]) * scale
            last_extra = total_w if c1 + 1 == n else 0.0
            if c1 > c and nw + last_extra > max_w:
                break
            w, c1 = nw, c1 + 1
        last = c1 == n
        out.append(Group(c, c1, first, last, w + (total_w if last else 0.0)))
        c = c1
    return out


def merge_groups(ds: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Join group answers left to right: values and small totals concatenate; row totals and grand come from the last."""
    rows = {r: {"values": [v for d in ds for v in d["rows"][r]["values"]], "total": ds[-1]["rows"][r]["total"]}
            for r in ROWS}
    return {"contest": ds[0].get("contest"), "candidate": ds[0].get("candidate"), "rows": rows,
            "col_totals": [v for d in ds for v in d["col_totals"]], "grand": ds[-1]["grand"]}


def group_image(hi_png, b, edges, g, scale, dest: Path) -> Path:
    """Stitch the strips of one group side by side: labels | columns | TOTAL, all the block's full height."""
    y0, y1 = round(b.y0 * scale), round(b.y1 * scale)
    xs = [(b.x0, edges[0])] if g.labels else []
    xs.append((edges[g.c0], edges[g.c1]))
    if g.total:
        xs.append((edges[-1], b.x1))
    with Image.open(hi_png) as im:
        strips = [im.crop((round(a * scale), y0, round(z * scale), y1)) for a, z in xs]
    out = Image.new(strips[0].mode, (sum(s.width for s in strips), y1 - y0), 255)
    x = 0
    for s in strips:
        out.paste(s, (x, 0))
        x += s.width
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.save(dest)
    return dest


def _int_or_none(v, what):
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool)):
        return v
    raise ValueError(f"{what} must be an integer or null, got {v!r}")


def _check_list(vals, n, what):
    if not isinstance(vals, list) or len(vals) != n:
        raise ValueError(f"{what} must be a list of {n} entries, got "
                         f"{len(vals) if isinstance(vals, list) else type(vals).__name__}")
    for v in vals:
        _int_or_none(v, what)


def validator(n: int, rows=ROWS, extra=()):
    def check(d):
        if not isinstance(d, dict) or not isinstance(d.get("rows"), dict):
            raise ValueError("answer must be an object with a 'rows' object")
        for r in rows + tuple(extra):
            if r not in d["rows"]:
                raise ValueError(f"row {r} is missing")
            _check_list(d["rows"][r].get("values"), n, f"{r} values")
            _int_or_none(d["rows"][r].get("total"), f"{r} total")
        _check_list(d.get("col_totals"), n, "col_totals")
        _int_or_none(d.get("grand"), "grand")
    return check


def header_validator(d):
    p = d.get("precincts")
    if not isinstance(p, list) or not p:
        raise ValueError("precincts must be a non-empty list")
    d["precincts"] = [str(x).strip() for x in p]
    if len(set(d["precincts"])) != len(d["precincts"]):
        raise ValueError("precinct labels must be distinct")
    n = len(p)
    _check_list(d.get("registered", {}).get("values"), n, "registered values")
    validator(n)(d)


def _edges(blocks, n):
    """Column edges for a page: from the first block with n+2 lines: the left edge of the row-label box, then the n+1
    precinct edges (the last is TOTAL's left edge). Returns those n+1 edges."""
    for b in blocks:
        if len(b.lines) == n + 2:
            return b.lines[1:n + 2]
    return None


def _box(edges, b, row_i, col_i):
    if edges is None:
        return (None,) * 4
    h = (b.rule_y1 - b.rule_y0) / len(ROWS)
    return (edges[col_i], round(b.rule_y0 + row_i * h), edges[col_i + 1], round(b.rule_y0 + (row_i + 1) * h))


def _store(led, county, page, bid, d, cols, contest, candidate, model, edges, b):
    """Write one block's answer: cells (null = blacked out, no cell) and printed totals. Returns cells stored."""
    stored = 0
    for ri, r in enumerate(ROWS):
        for ci, col in enumerate(cols):
            v = d["rows"][r]["values"][ci]
            if v is None:
                continue
            led.put_cell(county, page, bid, r, col, v, contest=contest, candidate=candidate, model=model,
                         box=_box(edges, b, ri, ci) if edges else (None,) * 4)
            stored += 1
        if d["rows"][r]["total"] is not None:
            led.put_total(county, page, bid, "row", r, d["rows"][r]["total"])
    for ci, col in enumerate(cols):
        if d["col_totals"][ci] is not None:
            led.put_total(county, page, bid, "col", col, d["col_totals"][ci])
    if d["grand"] is not None:
        led.put_total(county, page, bid, "grand", "", d["grand"])
    return stored


def _store_header(led, county, page, d, cols, model):
    n = 0
    for ci, col in enumerate(cols):
        led.put_cell(county, page, "reg", "REGISTERED", col, d["registered"]["values"][ci], contest="Registered voters",
                     model=model)
        n += 1
    if d["registered"].get("total") is not None:
        led.put_total(county, page, "reg", "row", "REGISTERED", d["registered"]["total"])
    n += _store(led, county, page, "cast", d, cols, "Ballots cast", None, model, None, None)
    return n


def summarize(led, county):
    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
    rows, cols, grand = (checks.row_checks(cells, totals), checks.column_checks(cells, totals),
                         checks.grand_checks(totals))
    ok = lambda cs: sum(c.ok for c in cs)
    return {"cells_read": len(cells), "failed_cells": sum(c["status"] == "failed" for c in cells),
            "row_sums_pass": ok(rows), "row_sums_fail": len(rows) - ok(rows),
            "col_sums_pass": ok(cols), "col_sums_fail": len(cols) - ok(cols),
            "grand_sums_pass": ok(grand), "grand_sums_fail": len(grand) - ok(grand),
            "printed_totals": len(totals)}


def _read_block(gw, county, page, bid, b, edges, cols, png, crop_path, run_id, root, dpi):
    """One answer for the block: one call on the whole crop when the page gives no column edges, else one per group."""
    if edges is None:
        g = Group(0, len(cols), True, True, b.x1 - b.x0)
        return gw.ask_json(block_prompt(g, cols), crop_path, validate=validator(len(cols)))
    scale = READ_DPI / dpi
    hi = page_png(county, page, READ_DPI, root)
    groups = plan_groups(edges, b.x0, b.x1, scale=scale, max_w=MAX_WIDTH)
    answers = []
    for k, g in enumerate(groups):
        path = group_image(hi, b, edges, g, scale,
                           Path("runs") / run_id / "crops" / f"{bid}-g{k}.png" if run_id else Path(f"/tmp/{bid}-g{k}.png"))
        with Image.open(path) as im:
            w, h = im.size
        before = gw.cost
        with tracing.trace("read_group", kind="TOOL", run=run_id, county=county, page=page, block=bid, group=k,
                           col_first=g.c0, col_last=g.c1 - 1, crop_width=w, crop_height=h, dpi=READ_DPI) as sp:
            answers.append(gw.ask_json(block_prompt(g, cols[g.c0:g.c1]), path, validate=validator(g.c1 - g.c0)))
            sp.set_attribute("estimated_cost_usd", round(gw.cost - before, 5))
    return merge_groups(answers)


def _rows_in(led, county):
    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
    chs = checks.row_checks(cells, totals)
    return len(chs), sum(1 for c in chs if not c.ok)


def read_county(county, gw, led, *, run_id="", pages=None, dpi=200, log=print, data_root=None, model="auto") -> dict:
    """Read every page of a matrix-layout county block by block into the ledger. Returns the summary dict.

    model="auto": a sample of page 1 is read with claude-haiku first and the reader is chosen by the share of its row
    sums that fail (layouts/profile.py); the sample always comes from page 1, whatever `pages` says. Any other name
    reads the county with that model and skips the sample."""
    from ..sources import DATA
    from . import profile
    root = data_root or DATA
    t0 = time.time()
    pages = list(pages or range(1, 7))
    st = {"cols": None, "contest": None, "failed": 0, "log": [], "done": set()}
    stopped, sample = None, None
    blocks_of: dict = {}

    def blocks_for(page):
        if page not in blocks_of:
            blocks_of[page] = find_blocks(page_png(county, page, dpi, root))
        return blocks_of[page]

    def read_blocks(page, stop_when=None):
        """Read the blocks of one page not read yet. Stops early when `stop_when()` is true after a block."""
        png = page_png(county, page, dpi, root)
        blocks = blocks_for(page)
        for i, b in enumerate(blocks):
            bid = f"p{page}-b{i}"
            is_header = page == 1 and i == 0
            if bid in st["done"] or (page not in pages and not is_header and not stop_when):
                continue
            crop_path = Path("runs") / run_id / "crops" / f"{bid}.png" if run_id else Path(f"/tmp/{bid}.png")
            crop(png, b.box, crop_path)
            st["done"].add(bid)
            try:
                with tracing.trace("read_block", kind="TOOL", run=run_id, county=county, page=page, block=bid):
                    if is_header:
                        d = gw.ask_json(HEADER_PROMPT, crop_path, validate=header_validator)
                        st["cols"] = d["precincts"]
                        n = _store_header(led, county, page, d, st["cols"], gw.model)
                        what = "header"
                    else:
                        edges = _edges(blocks, len(st["cols"]))
                        d = _read_block(gw, county, page, bid, b, edges, st["cols"], png, crop_path, run_id, root, dpi)
                        st["contest"] = d.get("contest") or st["contest"]
                        n = _store(led, county, page, bid, d, st["cols"], st["contest"], d.get("candidate"), gw.model,
                                   edges, b)
                        what = d.get("candidate")
                led.event(county, "block_read", {"page": page, "block": bid, "cells": n, "candidate": what,
                                                 "model": gw.model})
                st["log"].append({"block": bid, "page": page, "status": "read", "cells": n, "candidate": what,
                                  "box": list(b.box)})
            except BudgetExceeded:
                raise
            except Exception as e:  # bad JSON twice, wrong shape, or a model error: mark the block failed, go on
                st["failed"] += 1
                if st["cols"]:
                    for r in ROWS:
                        for col in st["cols"]:
                            led.put_cell(county, page, bid, r, col, None, model=gw.model)
                            led.set_status(county, page, bid, r, col, "failed")
                led.event(county, "block_failed", {"page": page, "block": bid, "error": str(e)[:300]})
                st["log"].append({"block": bid, "page": page, "status": "failed", "error": str(e)[:300]})
                log(f"  {bid}: failed ({str(e)[:100]})")
                if is_header:
                    raise RuntimeError("the page-1 header could not be read; later pages need its precinct order")
            if stop_when and stop_when():
                return

    try:
        with tracing.trace("read_county", kind="WORKFLOW", run=run_id, county=county):
            # the header row is printed on page 1 only (checked by eye); later pages reuse its precinct order
            if model == "auto":
                gw.model = profile.SAMPLE_MODEL
                read_blocks(1, stop_when=lambda: _rows_in(led, county)[0] >= profile.SAMPLE_ROW_SUMS)
                with tracing.trace("choose_reader", kind="TOOL", run=run_id, county=county) as sp:
                    total, failing = _rows_in(led, county)
                    sample = profile.decide(failing, total)
                    sample["blocks"] = sorted(st["done"])
                    for k in ("row_sums", "failing", "rate", "reader", "kept_sample"):
                        sp.set_attribute(f"sample_{k}" if k != "reader" else "choice", sample[k])
                led.event(county, "choose_reader", sample)
                log(profile.sentence(sample))
                gw.model = sample["reader"]
                if not sample["kept_sample"]:
                    led.clear_values(county)
                    st.update(cols=None, contest=None, failed=0, log=[], done=set())
            else:
                gw.model = model
                sample = {"reader": model, "skipped": True, "kept_sample": False}
                led.event(county, "choose_reader", sample)
                log(f"reader: {model} (set with --model; no sample was read)")
            for page in sorted(set(pages) | {1}):
                read_blocks(page)
    except BudgetExceeded as e:
        stopped = str(e)
        log(f"stopped: {e}")
    s = summarize(led, county)
    found = sum(len(blocks_for(p)) for p in pages)
    s.update(county=county, run_id=run_id, blocks_found=found, blocks_failed=st["failed"], reader=gw.model,
             sample=sample, precincts=st["cols"], model_calls=gw.calls, prompt_tokens=gw.prompt_tokens,
             completion_tokens=gw.completion_tokens, metered_cost_estimate=round(gw.cost, 4),
             seconds=round(time.time() - t0, 1), stopped=stopped, blocks=st["log"])
    return s


# ---- where things are on the page (for re-reads and for the results page); boxes are in 200 dpi pixels ----

HEADER_ROWS = ("REGISTERED",) + ROWS + ("SMALL",)   # page 1's first block: one more row, and its small
# totals sit inside the ruled box, as its last row
GEO_DPI = 200
PAD = 8             # pixels of page around a crop, at 200 dpi
SMALL_ROW = 30      # height of the row of small printed totals under the ruled rows, at 200 dpi
MIN_DIGIT_PX = 40   # a re-read crop is enlarged until its digits are at least this tall
# printed digit height at 200 dpi, measured by eye on the Panola scan: cells and large totals about 10 px, the small
# totals about 6 px
DIGIT_200 = {"cell": 10, "row_total": 10, "grand": 10, "col_total": 6, "column": 6}


def digit_px(dpi: int, kind: str) -> float:
    return DIGIT_200[kind] * dpi / GEO_DPI


def scale_for(dpi: int, kind: str) -> float:
    return max(1.0, round(MIN_DIGIT_PX / digit_px(dpi, kind) + 0.01, 2))


class GeometryError(Exception):
    pass


class Geometry:
    """Boxes of cells, printed totals and blocks of one matrix-layout county, and crops of them from the scan."""

    def __init__(self, county, cols, root=None):
        from ..sources import DATA
        self.county, self.cols, self.root = county, list(cols), root or DATA
        self._pages: dict = {}
        self._rule_cache: dict = {}
        self._cur_page = None

    def _page(self, page):
        if page not in self._pages:
            blocks = find_blocks(page_png(self.county, page, GEO_DPI, self.root))
            self._pages[page] = (blocks, _edges(blocks, len(self.cols)))
        return self._pages[page]

    def _block(self, page, bid):
        blocks, edges = self._page(page)
        i = 0 if bid in ("reg", "cast") else int(bid.rsplit("-b", 1)[1])
        if i >= len(blocks) or edges is None:
            raise GeometryError(f"no column lines found for {bid} on page {page}")
        rows = HEADER_ROWS if bid in ("reg", "cast") else ROWS
        self._cur_page = page
        self._rules(blocks[i], edges)
        return blocks[i], edges, rows

    def _rules(self, b, edges):
        """y of each horizontal rule across the precinct columns inside the block's ruled height, found in the image."""
        key = (b.y0, b.x0)
        if key not in self._rule_cache:
            import numpy as np
            png = page_png(self.county, self._cur_page, GEO_DPI, self.root)
            with Image.open(png) as im:
                g = np.asarray(im.convert("L"))[b.rule_y0 - 3:b.rule_y1 + 4, edges[0]:edges[-2]]
            cover = (g < 110).mean(axis=1) >= 0.6
            ys = []
            for s_, e_ in segment._runs(cover):
                ys.append(b.rule_y0 - 3 + (s_ + e_) // 2)
            self._rule_cache[key] = ys
        return self._rule_cache[key]

    def _row(self, b, rows, kind):
        i = rows.index(kind)
        ys = self._rule_cache.get((b.y0, b.x0)) or []
        h = (b.rule_y1 - b.rule_y0) / len(rows)

        def edge(j):    # an even split, moved onto a drawn rule when one lies within 5 px
            y = b.rule_y0 + j * h
            near = min(ys, key=lambda r: abs(r - y), default=None)
            return round(near if near is not None and abs(near - y) <= 5 else y)
        return edge(i), edge(i + 1)

    def block_box(self, page, bid):
        try:
            return self._block(page, bid)[0].box
        except GeometryError:
            return None

    def cell_box(self, page, bid, row, col):
        b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
        y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, row)
        ci = self.cols.index(col)
        return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], y1)

    def total_box(self, page, bid, direction, key):
        try:
            b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
            n = len(self.cols)
            if direction == "row":
                y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, key)
                return (edges[n], y0, b.x1, y1)
            if bid == "reg":
                return None
            if direction == "col":
                ci = self.cols.index(key)
                if bid == "cast":
                    y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, "SMALL")
                    return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], y1)
                return (edges[ci], b.rule_y1, edges[ci + 1], min(b.y1, b.rule_y1 + SMALL_ROW))
            if bid == "cast":
                y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, "SMALL")
                return (edges[n], y0, b.x1, b.y1)
            return (edges[n], b.rule_y1, b.x1, b.y1)
        except (GeometryError, ValueError):
            return None

    def target_box(self, page, bid, t):
        """The box of a re-read target, without padding."""
        b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
        kind = t["kind"]
        if kind == "cell":
            return self.cell_box(page, bid, t["row"], t["column"])
        if kind == "column":
            ci = self.cols.index(t["column"])
            y0 = self._row(b, rows, "EARLY")[0]
            if bid == "cast":
                return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], self._row(b, rows, "SMALL")[1])
            return (edges[ci], y0, edges[ci + 1], min(b.y1, b.rule_y1 + SMALL_ROW))
        if kind == "row_total":
            return self.total_box(page, bid, "row", t["row"])
        if kind == "col_total":
            return self.total_box(page, bid, "col", t["column"])
        if kind == "grand":
            return self.total_box(page, bid, "grand", "")
        raise GeometryError(f"unknown target kind {kind!r}")

    def crop(self, page, bid, t, dpi, dest: Path):
        """Cut the target out of the page at `dpi`, with padding, enlarged so its digits are at least 40 px tall.
        Returns (path, box at 200 dpi)."""
        try:
            box = self.target_box(page, bid, t)
        except ValueError:
            box = None
        if box is None:
            raise GeometryError(f"cannot place {t} in {bid} on page {page}")
        return self._cut(page, box, t["kind"], dpi, dest), box

    def _cut(self, page, box, kind, dpi, dest: Path) -> Path:
        k = dpi / GEO_DPI
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = box
        with Image.open(page_png(self.county, page, dpi, self.root)) as im:
            win = (max(0, round((x0 - PAD) * k)), max(0, round((y0 - PAD) * k)),
                   min(im.width, round((x1 + PAD) * k)), min(im.height, round((y1 + PAD) * k)))
            c = im.crop(win)
        s = scale_for(dpi, kind)
        if s > 1:
            c = c.resize((round(c.width * s), round(c.height * s)), Image.LANCZOS)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        c.save(dest)
        return dest

    def strip_crops(self, page, bid, row, dpi, dest: Path, per: int = 7):
        """One row of one block cut into pieces of at most `per` cells. Returns [(path, [precincts], box at 200 dpi)]."""
        try:
            b, edges, rows = self._block(page, bid)
            if row not in rows:
                raise GeometryError(f"no row {row} in {bid}")
            y0, y1 = self._row(b, rows, row)
            out = []
            for i in range(0, len(self.cols), per):
                cols = self.cols[i:i + per]
                box = (edges[i], y0, edges[i + len(cols)], y1)
                out.append((self._cut(page, box, "cell", dpi, dest.with_name(f"{dest.stem}-s{i // per}{dest.suffix}")),
                            cols, box))
            return out
        except (ValueError, IndexError):
            raise GeometryError(f"cannot place row {row} in {bid} on page {page}") from None


def precinct_order(led, county) -> list[str]:
    """The precinct columns left to right, as the header block's registered-voters row was read."""
    seen = []
    for c in led.cells(county):
        if c["block_id"] == "reg" and c["column"] not in seen:
            seen.append(c["column"])
    return seen

48	def row_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
49	    """One check per (page, block, row_kind) that has a printed row total: the row's cells must add to it."""
50	    printed = _printed(totals, "row")

55	    return [_make("row", *k, g, printed[k], (k[0], k[1], "row", k[2]), ONE_SUM if k[2] == "REGISTERED" else "")

61	    printed = _printed(totals, "col")
62	    groups: dict = {}

68	def grand_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:

70	    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
71	    out = []

73	        cols = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "col" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block]
74	        terms = [((page, block, "col", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in cols]
75	        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)

80	def grand_row_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
81	    """The printed row totals of a block must add to its printed grand total (kind 'grand_row'). The registered-voters
82	    row is not a term: it is not a count of ballots."""
83	    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
84	    out = []
85	    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
86	        rows = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "row" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block and
87	                t["key"] != "REGISTERED"]
88	        if not rows:
89	            continue
90	        terms = [((page, block, "row", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in rows]
91	        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
92	        out.append(Check("grand_row", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g, (page, block, "grand", "")))

96	def grid_gaps(cells: list[dict]) -> list[tuple]:
97	    """Cell keys that are absent or unread where the block's grid says they should be.
98	
99	    Within a block the grid is every row_kind crossed with every column that appears in it.
100	    Returns sorted (page, block_id, row_kind, column) tuples.
101	    """
102	    blocks: dict = {}
103	    for c in cells:
104	        b = blocks.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"]), {"rows": set(), "cols": set(), "have": set()})
105	        b["rows"].add(c["row_kind"]); b["cols"].add(c["column"])
106	        if c["value"] is not None:
107	            b["have"].add((c["row_kind"], c["column"]))
108	    return sorted((p, bid, r, col) for (p, bid), b in blocks.items()
109	                  for r in b["rows"] for col in b["cols"] if (r, col) not in b["have"])

112	def locate(rows: list[Check], cols: list[Check]) -> list[tuple]:
113	    """Cell keys that sit on a failing row sum and on a failing column sum at once."""
114	    bad_rows = {k for ch in rows if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
115	    bad_cols = {k for ch in cols if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
116	    return sorted(bad_rows & bad_cols)

120	    return row_checks(cells, totals) + column_checks(cells, totals) + grand_checks(totals) + grand_row_checks(totals)

123	@dataclass
124	class Suspect:
125	    entity: tuple     # a cell key (page, block, row_kind, column) or a printed total (page, block, 'row'|'col'|'grand', key)
126	    read: int         # the value now in the ledger
127	    would_be: int     # the value both of its sums need
128	    error: int        # read - would_be
129	    sums: tuple       # the two failing Checks it sits on
130

132	@dataclass
133	class Located:
134	    suspects: list = field(default_factory=list)
135	    unlocated: list = field(default_factory=list)   # [(Check, why)]: failing sums no single value explains
136	
137	
138	def suspects(chs: list[Check]) -> Located:
139	    """Pair failing sums. A value that sits on exactly two failing sums, and is off by the same amount on both (the sign
140	    its place in each sum gives), is a suspect, and the value both sums need is `would_be`. A value read too high by e
141	    makes a sum it is a term of too high by e, and a sum it is the printed total of too low by e. Pure arithmetic:
142	    it says where to look, never what to write. A failing sum that no unique suspect explains is `unlocated`, with the
143	    reason (an unread term, one sum only, more than one candidate, or differences that do not pair)."""
144	    failing = [c for c in chs if not c.ok]
145	    out = Located()
146	    on: dict = {}                                  # entity -> [(Check, error it implies, value)]
147	    unread = []
148	    for c in failing:
149	        if c.computed is None or c.printed is None:
150	            unread.append(c)
151	            continue
152	        d = c.computed - c.printed
153	        for k, v in c.terms:
154	            on.setdefault(k, []).append((c, d, v))
155	        if c.printed_key is not None:
156	            on.setdefault(c.printed_key, []).append((c, -d, c.printed))
157	    cand = []
158	    for e, lst in on.items():
159	        if len(lst) == 2 and lst[0][1] == lst[1][1] != 0 and lst[0][2] - lst[0][1] >= 0:
160	            cand.append(Suspect(e, lst[0][2], lst[0][2] - lst[0][1], lst[0][1], (lst[0][0], lst[1][0])))
161	    uses: dict = {}
162	    for s in cand:
163	        for c in s.sums:
164	            uses[id(c)] = uses.get(id(c), 0) + 1
165	    out.suspects = [s for s in cand if all(uses[id(c)] == 1 for c in s.sums)]
166	    explained = {id(c) for s in out.suspects for c in s.sums}
167	    for c in failing:
168	        if id(c) in explained:
169	            continue
170	        if c in unread:
171	            why = "a term is unread"
172	        elif c.note:
173	            why = f"one sum only: {c.note}"
174	        elif uses.get(id(c), 0) > 1:
175	            why = "more than one value could be the one: several pairs of failing sums agree"
176	        else:
177	            why = "its difference cannot be paired with another failing sum (two or more wrong values may share it)"
178	        out.unlocated.append((c, why))
179	    return out
180	
181	
182	def crossing(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> dict:
183	    """For each cell key, the row and column checks it sits on (a cell on no printed sum maps to an empty list)."""
184	    on: dict = {cell_key(c): [] for c in cells if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN}
185	    for ch in row_checks(cells, totals) + column_checks(cells, totals):
186	        for k, _ in ch.terms:
187	            on[k].append(ch)
188	    return on

1	"""The investigation loop: pairing finds where to look, re-reads of the scan decide, code holds it to the rules.
2	
3	Every printed value sits on two sums (see `checks.suspects`). A value that sits on two failing sums whose differences
4	agree is a suspect: it is re-read at 400 dpi or more with the county's reader, then one step up the ladder, and the
5	value changes only because a re-read gave the value both sums need. The same reading twice while both sums still
6	fail is `document_inconsistent`. A failing sum that pairing cannot place goes to `claude-sonnet-4.6`, which is shown
7	the sum in words and what has been tried, and answers with one JSON action: `reread` (one or more targets),
8	`cannot_verify` (a reason) or `done`. Code carries the action out and answers with the checks' new result. A model never
9	sets a status: a cell is accepted when every printed sum it sits on holds, and only then.
10	
11	Rules that code enforces whatever the model says:
12	- at most MAX_ACTIONS actions per item (a refused request counts as one);
13	- the ladder: the county's reader first, then `claude-sonnet-4.6`, then `claude-opus-4.6`; a step is allowed on a target
14	  only after the step below has been tried on it (and failed to settle it); model names are matched after trimming and
15	  lower-casing, and an unknown name falls back to the next step of the ladder;
16	- the same target is never re-read twice with the same model and dpi (a refusal, and it counts as an action);
17	- a cell that is already accepted is never re-read; a total is re-read only while a sum it sits on fails;
18	- a re-read value replaces the old one only if more of that value's sums hold with it; both readings are kept in the event;
19	- when an item stops, only the cells that pairing or the model could not clear become cannot_verify (a cell whose other
20	  sum holds is not marked); every sum still failing at the end has a verdict and a reason.
21	"""

169	def settle(led, county, updates: list[dict], seen: dict | None = None) -> list[dict]:
170	    """Decide for each proposed new value whether it replaces the old one: it does only if more of the sums it sits on
171	    hold with it than with the old value, the other proposed values being taken as they are. Writes the kept values.
172	    Each update: {entity: ('cell', page, block, row, col) | ('total', page, block, direction, key), old, new}.
173	    `seen` maps an entity to the values earlier re-reads gave it. Returns the updates with 'kept' ('new' | 'old' |
174	    'same') added."""
175	    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
176	
177	    def with_values(chosen):
178	        cs = [dict(c) for c in cells]
179	        ts = [dict(t) for t in totals]
180	        for u, v in chosen:
181	            e = u["entity"]
182	            if e[0] == "cell":
183	                for c in cs:
184	                    if _ckey(c) == tuple(e[1:]):
185	                        c["value"] = v
186	            else:
187	                for t in ts:
188	                    if (t["page"], t["block_id"], t["direction"], t["key"]) == tuple(e[1:]):
189	                        t["value"] = v
190	        return cs, ts
191	
192	    live = [u for u in updates if u["new"] is not None and u["new"] != u["old"]]
193	    all_new = [(u, u["new"]) for u in live]
194	    for u in updates:
195	        if u not in live:
196	            u["kept"] = "same"
197	            continue
198	        reverted = [(x, x["old"] if x is u else x["new"]) for x in live]
199	        n_new = _holding(u["entity"], *with_values(all_new))
200	        n_old = _holding(u["entity"], *with_values(reverted))
201	        # a tie goes to the old value, unless an earlier re-read of the same thing already gave this new value
202	        agreed = seen is not None and u["new"] in seen.get(u["entity"], ())
203	        u["kept"] = "new" if n_new > n_old or (n_new == n_old and agreed) else "old"
204	        u["agreed"] = agreed
205	        u["sums_hold_new"], u["sums_hold_old"] = n_new, n_old
206	    for u in updates:
207	        e = u["entity"]
208	        if e[0] == "cell":
209	            keep = u["new"] if u.get("kept") == "new" else u["old"]
210	            led.reread_cell(county, e[1], e[2], e[3], e[4], keep, u["model"] if u.get("kept") == "new" else None)
211	        elif u.get("kept") == "new":
212	            led.put_total(county, e[1], e[2], e[3], e[4], u["new"])
213	    return updates

282	    if me.kind.startswith("grand"):
283	        return "Note: the small totals do not add to the grand total; either a small total or the grand total is misread."

288	    cells, totals, chs = _state(led, county)
289	    me = next((c for c in chs if _ck(c) == (item.kind, item.page, item.block, item.key)), None)
290	    others = _crossing_checks(item, chs)

292	    title = (f"page {item.page}, block {item.block}"
293	             f"{', ' + str(who['contest']) if who and who.get('contest') else ''}"

307	    ladder = list(ladder)

345	def read_validator(kind, n=None):
346	    def check(d):
347	        if not isinstance(d, dict):
348	            raise ValueError("answer must be an object")
349	        if kind == "row_strip":
350	            v = d.get("values")
351	            if not isinstance(v, list) or len(v) != n:
352	                raise ValueError(f"values must be a list of {n} entries")
353	            for x in v:
354	                if x is not None:
355	                    _int(x, "value")
356	        elif kind == "column":
357	            for k in (*ROWS, "total"):
358	                _int(d.get(k), k)
359	        else:
360	            _int(d.get("value"), "value")
361	    return check

364	def decision_validator(d):
365	    if not isinstance(d, dict) or d.get("action") not in ("reread", "cannot_verify", "done"):
366	        raise ValueError('"action" must be "reread", "cannot_verify" or "done"')
367	    if d["action"] == "cannot_verify" and not str(d.get("reason") or "").strip():
368	        raise ValueError('"cannot_verify" needs a "reason"')
369	    if d["action"] != "reread":
370	        return
371	    rr = d.get("rereads")
372	    if rr is None and "target" in d:
373	        rr = [{k: d[k] for k in ("target", "dpi", "model") if k in d}]
374	    if not isinstance(rr, list) or not rr:
375	        raise ValueError('"reread" needs a non-empty "rereads" list')
376	    norm = []
377	    for r in rr:
378	        t = r.get("target") if isinstance(r, dict) else None
379	        if not isinstance(t, dict) or t.get("kind") not in KINDS:
380	            raise ValueError(f"target kind must be one of {KINDS}")
381	        need = {"cell": ("row", "column"), "column": ("column",), "row_total": ("row",), "col_total": ("column",),
382	                "grand": (), "row_strip": ("row",)}[t["kind"]]
383	        for f in need:
384	            if not isinstance(t.get(f), str) or not t[f]:
385	                raise ValueError(f'target {t["kind"]} needs "{f}"')
386	        dpi = r.get("dpi", 300)
387	        if dpi not in DPIS:
388	            raise ValueError(f"dpi must be one of {DPIS}")
389	        model = r.get("model") or ""
390	        if not isinstance(model, str):
391	            raise ValueError("model must be a name")
392	        norm.append({"target": {k: t[k] for k in ("kind", *need)}, "dpi": dpi, "model": model})  # unknown names: pick_model
393	    d["rereads"] = norm

440	        made to hold, so they are not worked again."""
441	        out = {_ckey(c) for c in self.led.cells(self.county) if c["status"] in FINAL}

448	    def _target_refusal(self, item, t):
449	        """The reason this target may not be re-read now, else None."""
450	        cells, totals, chs = _state(self.led, self.county)
451	        page, bid = item.page, item.block
452	        byk = {_ckey(c): c for c in cells}
453	        failing = {_ck(c) for c in chs if not c.ok}
454	        kind = t["kind"]
455	        if kind == "cell":
456	            c = byk.get((page, bid, t["row"], t["column"]))
457	            if c is None:
458	                return f"there is no cell {t['row']} / {t['column']} in {bid}"
459	            if c["status"] == "accepted":
460	                return "that cell is accepted: every sum it sits on holds"
461	        elif kind == "column":
462	            col = [c for c in cells if c["page"] == page and c["block_id"] == bid and c["column"] == t["column"]]
463	            if not col:
464	                return f"there is no column {t['column']} in {bid}"
465	            if all(c["status"] == "accepted" for c in col) and ("col", page, bid, t["column"]) not in failing:
466	                return "every cell of that column is accepted"
467	        elif kind == "row_strip":
468	            row = [c for c in cells if c["page"] == page and c["block_id"] == bid and c["row_kind"] == t["row"]]
469	            if not row:
470	                return f"there is no row {t['row']} in {bid}"
471	            if all(c["status"] == "accepted" for c in row):
472	                return "every cell of that row is accepted"
473	        elif kind == "row_total":
474	            if ("row", page, bid, t["row"]) not in failing and ("grand_row", page, bid, "") not in failing:
475	                return "that row's sum and the grand total by rows hold; its printed total is not in question"
476	        elif kind == "col_total":
477	            if ("col", page, bid, t["column"]) not in failing and ("grand_col", page, bid, "") not in failing:
478	                return "that column's sum and the grand total hold; the small total is not in question"
479	        elif kind == "grand":
480	            if ("grand_col", page, bid, "") not in failing and ("grand_row", page, bid, "") not in failing:
481	                return "the grand total's sums hold"

488	    def _updates(self, item, t, ans, model):
489	        page, bid = item.page, item.block
490	        cells = {_ckey(c): c for c in self.led.cells(self.county)}
491	        out = []
492	        if t["kind"] in ("cell", "column", "row_strip"):
493	            if t["kind"] == "cell":
494	                pairs = [(t["row"], t["column"], ans["value"])]
495	            elif t["kind"] == "column":
496	                pairs = [(r, t["column"], ans[r]) for r in ROWS]
497	            else:
498	                pairs = [(t["row"], col, v) for col, v in ans["strip"].items() if v is not None]
499	            for r, col, v in pairs:
500	                c = cells.get((page, bid, r, col))
501	                if c is None or c["status"] == "accepted":
502	                    continue
503	                out.append({"entity": ("cell", page, bid, r, col), "old": c["value"], "new": v, "model": model,
504	                            "label": f"{r}/{col}"})
505	        if t["kind"] == "column" or t["kind"] == "col_total":
506	            out.append({"entity": ("total", page, bid, "col", t["column"]),
507	                        "old": self._total(page, bid, "col", t["column"]),
508	                        "new": ans["total"] if t["kind"] == "column" else ans["value"], "model": model,
509	                        "label": f"small total/{t['column']}"})
510	        if t["kind"] == "row_total":
511	            out.append({"entity": ("total", page, bid, "row", t["row"]), "old": self._total(page, bid, "row", t["row"]),
512	                        "new": ans["value"], "model": model, "label": f"row total/{t['row']}"})
513	        if t["kind"] == "grand":
514	            out.append({"entity": ("total", page, bid, "grand", ""), "old": self._total(page, bid, "grand", ""),
515	                        "new": ans["value"], "model": model, "label": "grand total"})
516	        return out

520	        item.history.append(f"asked for {_tdesc(t)} with {model}: refused ({why})")
